purpose: Records the relock of the OpenHands recipe lock (blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/requirements.lock) from PyJWT 2.13.0 to 2.14.0. Nine PyJWT advisories published on 2026-09-29 (one Critical, five High, three Medium) failed the required osv-scanner check on the lock, and a tenth, GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq, had been ignored until 2026-10-13; OSV and GitHub list 2.14.0 as the first patched release for all ten. The change removes that ignore and its IGNORE_SCOPES entry and rebinds the lock's IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry to the relocked sha256 for the two oauthlib advisories it still needs, carrying the 2026-09-29 reachability review forward at the new digest. The 2026-09-29 record planned one relock onto oauthlib 4.0.0 and PyJWT 2.14.0; this record does the PyJWT half and gives the reason for leaving oauthlib at 3.3.1.
authorization: The lock's owner session (token-save-practice-e2e-status) could not be reached on 2026-09-29 and is gone (session 21, 2026-09-30). The Gate A owner (2d) and the pi-practice session (a2) each asked the coordinator for this relock; session 21 claimed it, then withdrew and reviewed this record.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's config and the workflow's command line, a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv (a host install check on the host network, with no model request: not the image, not an OpenHands run), requests-oauthlib 2.0.0's own unit tests run by us under two oauthlib versions (unchanged upstream test code on our scratch tree, section J), and reads of registry and advisory records (PyPI JSON API, OSV API, GitHub advisories API, the PyJWT 2.14.0 sdist and wheel). The diff and hash-equality comparisons are structural checks, not executions. The CI failure is read from the log of one run (gh run view --log-failed). Returned outputs: blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/evidence/relock-2026-09-30.txt.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock, which still pins PyJWT 2.13.0 (SDK@fcc102a, read from the pinned archive: section B of the returned outputs), and the 2026-09-28 grype record of that image predates these advisories, does not contain PyJWT and was not rerun. Which of the ten advisories reach the image's binary is unmeasured.

The grader venv is outside this lock. install-grader.sh syncs OpenHands/benchmarks@405bae7's uv.lock (digest equal to pins.json grader.uv_lock_sha256), which pins PyJWT 2.10.1 (section I). By the advisories' ranges (section H), 2.10.1 is affected by GHSA-2gx3-rcp4-g85q, GHSA-9v7f-9g4p-ffgj, GHSA-ffc3-869f-jxw9, GHSA-hxm8-2xgr-2p9m, GHSA-p4g4-x82p-q773 and GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq. That lock is not in .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json, so no check scans it; whether the grader path executes JWT code is unmeasured.

An existing recipe installation that recorded the old requirements_sha256 must re-run install (host.py install) before the next run: host.py:1432-1433 refuses with matching_successful_installation_required. This host has no installation record (checked 2026-09-30), so nothing here is affected.

No OpenHands task ran with the relocked venv. The install check ran the SDK's import check and uv pip check only, on the host network (the SDK import can trigger litellm's remote model-cost fetch, which falls back offline; the 2026-09-27 check ran under bwrap --unshare-net); the image installation, model behavior and any runtime path through PyJWT 2.14.0 are unmeasured.

oauthlib stays at 3.3.1. The 2026-09-29 non-reachability review of that pin is carried forward, not rerun (see carried_forward_review); its static text search shows which installed code references the vulnerable APIs, not a runtime trace, and read one hash-verified artifact per requirement, not every artifact the lock lists.

The OSV database is the live API at scan time. The clean result holds for 2026-09-30 only: an advisory published later for any pinned package fails the required check again. Every window statement in this record (oauthlib 4.0.0, PyJWT 2.15.0 and 2.15.1 inside the 7-day window) is as of 2026-09-30T03:46:13Z: PyJWT 2.15.0 leaves the window at 2026-09-30T16:56:01Z, oauthlib 4.0.0 at 2026-10-05T06:01:19Z and PyJWT 2.15.1 at 2026-10-05T18:40:43Z (each 7 days after the later of the release's file upload times on PyPI, fractional seconds rounded up to the next second).

One CI log was read (run 36657687493). The three main-branch push runs listed under ci_failure concluded failure and their logs were not read; the first two were created (23:33:17Z, 23:39:59Z) before the last two advisories were published (23:43:06Z, 23:43:19Z), so they most likely did not fail on all nine (the inference rests on the runs' createdAt, not their logs).

The 2.14.0 changelog names nine of the ten advisories. GHSA-9j54-fg26-wv3r (PyJWK accepts empty HMAC keys) is not named; its fix appears in the changelog's Fixed section as 'Reject empty HMAC keys when represented as JWKs', under GHSA-pxh4-856f-4h89, which GitHub's advisory API and OSV do not serve (404, as does GHSA-mvj7-wp6q-v59j, the changelog's other extra id). The claim that 2.14.0 fixes all ten rests on the OSV and GitHub ranges (all ten: first patched 2.14.0) and on the scan of the relocked tree, not on the changelog.

The PyJWT importer and caller search (section K) is a static text search of the installed .py files of the relocked venv: a name assembled at run time would not match, code the OpenHands agent writes and runs inside its container is out of scope, and it says where PyJWT's decode API is called, not what any run executed.
The tool's 'Filtered 7 vulnerabilities' count exceeds the six per-lock 'filtered out' lines it prints (oauthlib pair twice, nltk, setuptools); the two counts were not reconciled.

decision_point_2_15_0.reason_recorded_now: as of 2026-09-30T03:46:13Z: no decode of an attacker-controlled token through PyJWT is reachable in the recipe venv by static search of its 10,746 installed .py files (section K of the returned outputs). The venv's PyJWT importers are google-auth (oauth2/id_token.py:153 in verify_token, a module nothing outside google-auth imports), LiteLLM (its proxy server modules, not run by the recipe), oauthlib (common.py:221 verify_signed_token, no reference outside oauthlib), redis 7.2.1 (auth/token.py:89, a decode with verify_signature false of a token that a configured credential provider supplies; nothing outside redis references redis.auth.token or JWToken, and the recipe's own code imports neither redis nor jwt) and mcp 1.28.1 (jwt.encode of client assertions only). 2.15.0's Security item (recursion errors from deeply nested payloads wrapped in DecodeError, no advisory id) is the payload counterpart of GHSA-8wjv-2p76-3863, which 2.14.0 fixed for headers, so 2.14.0 most likely still raises a raw RecursionError on such a payload; that matters only where a decode of untrusted tokens is reachable, and none was found
decision_point_2_15_0.action_at_the_decision_point: confirm that reason still holds; if a decode of attacker-controlled JWTs has become reachable in the recipe venv, move the lock to 2.15.0 before the joint relock
